notes: Account: CollinsGate, midsize SaaS providing omnichannel support for B2B SaaS vendors.
Primary contact: VP Product - Aaron Collins. Product org evaluating chat agent to reduce CSAT cycle time.
Initial ask: streaming chat agent (SSE/websocket), tool calling for ticket lookups and account merges.
Latency requirement called out on kickoff: <1.5s first-token SLO for US production traffic; prefer p95 guarantee.
They want Hosted API for quick POC; likely commit to Dedicated if sustained peak capacity needed and pricing favorable.
Quoted sensitivity: care about per-token spend during nightly training jobs + daytime support peaks; want predictable committed pricing.
Security: must support enterprise SSO (SAML), audit logs, KMS integration; data residency for EU customers later.
Integrations: Zendesk + internal ticketing via tool-calling webhooks; lookups must be sub-200ms in-path.
Quote from Aaron on call: 'If we can't get under 1.5s for first bytes in streaming, ops won't sign off.'
SE note: will test with streaming + small prefix caching to validate first-token path; evaluate batching disabled for low-latency route.
Legal asked for sample DPA + encryption-at-rest statements; shared security FAQ (drive link).
Finance asked for ARR band and committed unit pricing scenarios for 12-month Dedicated contract.
Requested a demo of function/tool calling: show ticket fetch -> suggested reply -> submit as draft to Zendesk.
PD: wants deterministic fallbacks: if hosted model latency spikes, route to smaller quantized model in same API surface.
POC success criteria: avg time-to-resolution suggestion <= 30s, 95th percentile first-token <1.5s, cost per resolved conversation < $0.40.
Historical: trialed a different vendor last year; failed on latency during spikes (queueing/batching caused first-token >2.5s).
